title: Comparison dg functors for freely contracting a formal cone
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\mathcal A$ a small $R$-linear cochain dg category, and $u:x\to y$ a closed degree-zero arrow. Use the free adjoining constructions of [lem-coef-dgcat-free-cell-calculus] and the labelled cone enlargement of [lem-coef-dgcat-formal-cone-enlargement]. Let $\mathcal L$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Cone}(\mathcal A)$ on the labelled representables and $Z=C_u$. Let $\mathcal T=\mathcal L\langle h:Z\to Z,\ |h|=-1,\ dh=1_Z\rangle$, and let $\mathcal T_0$ be its full subcategory on the representable labels. Identify those labels with the objects of $\mathcal A$. Write $\iota_y,\pi_y,\iota_x,\pi_x$ for the graded cone inclusions and projections of degrees $0,0,-1,1$, respectively, and put
$$v_h=\pi_xh\iota_y,\quad a_h=\pi_xh\iota_x,\quad b_h=-\pi_yh\iota_y,\quad w_h=-\pi_yh\iota_x.$$

Let $\mathcal B$ be obtained from $\mathcal A$, without changing objects, by freely adjoining $v:y\to x$ of degree $0$, $a:x\to x$ and $b:y\to y$ of degree $-1$, and $w:x\to y$ of degree $-2$, with
$$dv=0,\quad da=vu-1_x,\quad db=uv-1_y,\quad dw=ua-bu.$$
There exist dg functors $F:\mathcal B\to\mathcal T_0$ and $G:\mathcal T_0\to\mathcal B$, identity on object labels and on the given $\mathcal A$ coefficients, such that
$$F(v)=v_h,\ F(a)=a_h,\ F(b)=b_h,\ F(w)=w_h,\qquad G(v_h)=v,\ G(a_h)=a,\ G(b_h)=b,\ G(w_h)=w.$$
More precisely, if $j:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ is the attaching functor, there is a dg functor $\widetilde G:\mathcal T\to\operatorname{Cone}(\mathcal B)$ whose restriction to $\mathcal L$ is the labelled cone extension of $j$, whose value on $h$ is the endomorphism of $C_{j(u)}$ with matrix
$$\begin{pmatrix}-b&-w\\ v&a\end{pmatrix},$$
and whose restriction on $\mathcal T_0$ is the representable embedding composed with $G$.

proof.text: Construct $\mathcal B$ by the successive free adjoining operations of [lem-coef-dgcat-free-cell-calculus], first $v$, then $a,b$, then $w$. The prescribed differentials are closed when they are attached: $d(vu-1_x)=d(uv-1_y)=0$ after adjoining $v$, and $d(ua-bu)=u(vu-1_x)-(uv-1_y)u=0$ after adjoining $a,b$. Thus the construction applies over the original ring $R$, leaves the objects unchanged, and gives the attaching dg functor $j:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$. The same operation applied to the closed identity $1_Z$ gives $\mathcal T$ and the dg inclusion of $\mathcal L$.

source.place: Tabuada, Chapter 1, section 1.3.1, Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29, comparison construction, with Proposition 1.7, printed p. 27. General closed-arrow case and the displayed cochain sign computations supplied by the agent.

proof.text:
For the four graded coordinate maps in $\mathcal L$, the module-map differential and the cone matrix of [lem-coef-dgcat-formal-cone-enlargement] give
$$d\iota_y=0,\qquad d\pi_x=0,\qquad d\iota_x=\iota_yu,\qquad d\pi_y=-u\pi_x.$$
Indeed $D_u\iota_y-\iota_yd_{h_y}=0$, $d_{h_x}\pi_x+\pi_xD_u=0$, $D_u\iota_x+\iota_xd_{h_x}=\iota_yu$, and $d_{h_y}\pi_y-\pi_yD_u=-u\pi_x$. These identities persist under the attaching dg functor into $\mathcal T$. The same cited statement gives $\pi_x\iota_y=\pi_y\iota_x=0$ and $\pi_x\iota_x=1_x$, $\pi_y\iota_y=1_y$.

source.place: Tabuada, Chapter 1, section 1.3.1, Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29, comparison construction, with Proposition 1.7, printed p. 27. General closed-arrow case and the displayed cochain sign computations supplied by the agent.

proof.text:
Compute in $\mathcal T$ by the signed Leibniz rule of [lem-coef-dgcat-free-cell-calculus], using step 2 and $dh=1_Z$. The degree of $\pi_x$ is $1$ and that of $h$ is $-1$, so
$$\begin{aligned}
dv_h&=-\pi_x\iota_y=0,\\
da_h&=-\pi_x\iota_x+\pi_xh\iota_yu=v_hu-1_x,\\
db_h&=u\pi_xh\iota_y-\pi_y\iota_y=uv_h-1_y,\\
dw_h&=u\pi_xh\iota_x-\pi_y\iota_x+\pi_yh\iota_yu=ua_h-b_hu.
\end{aligned}$$
All terms have endpoints among the representable labels, hence belong to the full dg subcategory $\mathcal T_0$. Their degrees are $0,-1,-1,-2$, respectively.

source.place: Tabuada, Chapter 1, section 1.3.1, Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29, comparison construction, with Proposition 1.7, printed p. 27. General closed-arrow case and the displayed cochain sign computations supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Use the free adjoining construction of [lem-coef-dgcat-free-cell-calculus] successively to extend the given $\mathcal A$ coefficient functor to $F:\mathcal B\to\mathcal T_0$, assigning $v,a,b,w$ the values $v_h,a_h,b_h,w_h$. Step 3 verifies each attaching differential. Explicitly, a word in old arrows and the four new generators is sent to the product of their assigned images, extended $R$-linearly; freeness makes this well defined, concatenation preserves composition and old units, and the Leibniz rule proves commutation with the differential on every word from the checked generator equations. The construction fixes every object label and the original $\mathcal A$ coefficients.

source.place: Tabuada, Chapter 1, section 1.3.1, Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29, comparison construction, with Proposition 1.7, printed p. 27. General closed-arrow case and the displayed cochain sign computations supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Apply the functorial labelled cone extension of [lem-coef-dgcat-formal-cone-enlargement] to $j:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and restrict it to $\mathcal L$. Denote this dg functor by $J:\mathcal L\to\operatorname{Cone}(\mathcal B)$. It sends $h_z$ to $h_{j(z)}$, sends $Z=C_u$ to $C_{j(u)}$, applies $j$ to the matrix entries, and sends the four coordinate maps to the corresponding four coordinate maps of $C_{j(u)}$. The last assertion follows directly from their coordinate matrices, whose entries are identities and zero maps.

source.place: Tabuada, Chapter 1, section 1.3.1, Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29, comparison construction, with Proposition 1.7, printed p. 27. General closed-arrow case and the displayed cochain sign computations supplied by the agent.

proof.text:
In $\operatorname{Cone}(\mathcal B)$ write $u$ for $j(u)$ and define the degree-$-1$ endomorphism
$$H=\begin{pmatrix}-b&-w\\ v&a\end{pmatrix}$$
of $C_{j(u)}$. The matrix degree convention of [lem-coef-dgcat-formal-cone-enlargement] requires entry degrees $(-1,-2;0,-1)$, which are precisely the degrees of these four entries. Its differential is $D_{j(u)}H+HD_{j(u)}$; multiplying the two matrices and collecting the original morphism differentials gives
$$dH=\begin{pmatrix}-db+uv&-dw+ua-bu\\-dv&vu-da\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1_y&0\\0&1_x\end{pmatrix}=1_{C_{j(u)}}.$$
The middle equality is exactly the four defining differential equations of $\mathcal B$ verified in step 1.

source.place: Tabuada, Chapter 1, section 1.3.1, Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29, comparison construction, with Proposition 1.7, printed p. 27. General closed-arrow case and the displayed cochain sign computations supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Now extend $J$ across the freely adjoined arrow $h$ by sending $h$ to $H$. The free adjoining operation of [lem-coef-dgcat-free-cell-calculus] applies since step 6 proves $dH=J(1_Z)$. It gives $\widetilde G:\mathcal T\to\operatorname{Cone}(\mathcal B)$ with the required restriction on $\mathcal L$. As in step 4, evaluate words in the old $\mathcal L$ arrows and $h$; their differential is preserved because it is preserved on $\mathcal L$ and on $h$. Thus this is a dg functor with the specified matrix value, rather than just an assignment of graded arrows.

source.place: Tabuada, Chapter 1, section 1.3.1, Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29, comparison construction, with Proposition 1.7, printed p. 27. General closed-arrow case and the displayed cochain sign computations supplied by the agent.

proof.text:
The restriction of $\widetilde G$ to $\mathcal T_0$ has only representable labels in its object image. For labels $z,t$ define $G$ on their morphism complex by composing $\widetilde G$ with the inverse of the isomorphism
$$\mathcal B(z,t)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(\mathcal B)(h_z,h_t)$$
from [lem-coef-dgcat-formal-cone-enlargement]. Those isomorphisms are isomorphisms of complexes preserving composition and units, so their inverses give a dg functor $G:\mathcal T_0\to\mathcal B$, identity on labels, with representable embedding composed with $G$ equal to $\widetilde G|_{\mathcal T_0}$. On an original coefficient $c\in\mathcal A(z,t)$ the entrywise formula for $J$ gives $G(c)=j(c)$, as required.

source.place: Tabuada, Chapter 1, section 1.3.1, Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29, comparison construction, with Proposition 1.7, printed p. 27. General closed-arrow case and the displayed cochain sign computations supplied by the agent.

proof.text:
Finally compute the images of the four displayed composites. By step 5 their coordinate factors go to the coordinate factors in $C_{j(u)}$, and by step 7 $h$ goes to $H$. Selecting the four matrix entries, with the two minus signs in the definitions of $b_h,w_h$, gives
$$\pi_xH\iota_y=v,\qquad \pi_xH\iota_x=a,\qquad -\pi_yH\iota_y=b,\qquad -\pi_yH\iota_x=w.$$
Here these equalities initially identify representable morphisms with the corresponding entries, using matrix composition and the full embedding of [lem-coef-dgcat-formal-cone-enlargement]. Applying the inverse isomorphisms used to define $G$ gives $G(v_h)=v$, $G(a_h)=a$, $G(b_h)=b$, $G(w_h)=w$. Together with step 4 these are every prescribed value, and step 7 supplies the more precise extension.
